1.2.3.11-f14.accuracy_reason: Sejanus was executed in AD 31 and his body was thrown down the Scalae Gemoniae.

1.2.3.11-f18.accuracy_reason: Plautus, Curculio 470ff.: the choragus's speech, which in standard texts reads 'ito in comitium' and 'Cloacinae sacrum'. The gloss on 'damnosos maritos' is fair.

1.2.3.11-f2.accuracy_reason: Confessions 11.29.39 reads 'dilaniantur cogitationes meae... tumultuosis varietatibus'; the note reports this correctly and hedges its account of the corruption.

1.2.3.11-f32.accuracy_reason: In Plutarch's Pyrrhus (ch. 14), Cineas argues that Pyrrhus can already have the leisure and feasting his conquests are meant to bring.

1.2.3.11-f6.accuracy_reason: Lucretius 3.995–7 is the political Sisyphus passage, ending 'semper victus tristisque recedit'.

1.2.3.11-f9.accuracy_reason: In Euripides, IA c. 450, Agamemnon complains that kings are slaves to the crowd. The note's doubt about Homer is properly hedged.
